Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **100**, STRONG BUY capitulation vs Regime state **69** with **4** risk-off signals, macro regime contraction at **70%**
The contrarian gauge measures how stretched sentiment is. The regime gauge measures where the economy and flows are heading. Trust the regime for direction and size, and use the contrarian reading only to time small starter positions.
⚠ These two disagree: VIX Spike tier **0** of **4**, backwardation flag off vs Two active confluences that both require VIX backwardation (T1 with HYG, T1 with JPY)
The confluences assume front-month VIX fear, while the spike detector sees baseline. One of them is wrong or early. Trust the spike detector for the VIX level today, and treat the confluences as a warning that the credit and yen legs are moving first.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite zone CALM vs Mother jaws score **100**
The composite counts how many pairs break from their normal link, and that count is **41.9%**, which is moderate. The jaws score measures how far the worst pairs have drifted, and that is extreme. Trust the jaws score for hidden stress, because a calm average can hide a few pairs that have fully flipped.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The call is defensive with a small contrarian hedge. The regime is contraction at 70% confidence, the regime score is 69 (transition), and 4 risk-off signals agree. The Crash Index sits at 3 of 10, which is the warning band.

The tension comes from the contrarian score. It reads 100, a full capitulation signal, while the VIX spike detector sits at tier 0 and the odds it gives for a spike are 50%. Sentiment is washed out, but nothing in volatility confirms a bottom. Prices fell over the last five days (Nasdaq 100 -2.9%, DAX -4.7%, Nikkei -7.7%) without a fear spike behind them.

For positioning, you keep gross exposure low and build any contrarian buys in small tranches. Credit stress and yen safe-haven flow are both active in the confluence list, so the first legs of a stress move are already under way. Cash and short-duration hedges earn their place while those two stay active.

The main risk is a fast squeeze from washed-out sentiment, so you do not short size into 100. What flips the stance is VIX backwardation turning on, which would move the spike tier off 0 and confirm the bear case. A turn in the regime score down from 69 into clear risk-off would do the same. A clean recovery in the Nikkei and DAX would take the stance back toward neutral.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is CONTRACTION at 70% confidence. In a contraction you keep exposure low, favor quality balance sheets and short duration, and avoid buying weakness before the credit and volatility readings confirm.

The contrarian score at 100 invites dip buying, and the regime says the dip can go deeper. A sensible split is a small starter position in the strongest areas, with most capital held back for a confirmed turn.

The regime would shift if the transition score of 69 moves up and the 4 risk-off signals drop out one by one.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together are now moving apart. Correlation drift is the size of that change, measured as the link between the two over a recent window against its longer-run norm.

The composite zone is calm. Of 43 pairs, 41.9% are diverging, with 13 leaning bullish and 5 leaning bearish, for a net bias of -8.

The mother jaws score reads 100, because the worst pairs have flipped fully. The 10-year minus 2-year yield curve moved from -0.61 to +0.40.

Gold and long bonds went from -0.56 to +0.78, so they now move together and the usual hedge between them has weakened. ARKK and the S&P 500 went from -0.01 to +0.71, which shows speculative growth tracking the index closely.

Transports against the Dow went from +0.48 to -0.49, and that split often shows up before a trend change. Six pairs share a score of 80.

You should treat the calm composite as an average that hides stress in a few key relationships, and size down any trade that relies on the old hedges.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

Two confluences are active: VIX backwardation with credit stress (HYG), and VIX backwardation with yen safe-haven flow. The third, VIX backwardation with small-cap drawdown, is off.

Both live signals point to funding and safe-haven stress, which are the places where trouble starts before equities react. Small caps are holding up best in the US (Russell 2000 -0.6% over five days), which fits that third signal staying quiet.

The lean is defensive: trim credit-sensitive and cyclical risk, keep hedges on, and watch whether small caps follow credit lower. A turn in HYG or a reversal in yen strength would remove the pressure.

The fact that the spike detector shows no backwardation today means these signals are early, so you cut risk gradually and do not liquidate.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Every region closed the five-day window lower, and the damage is larger the further east and the further into Europe you look. Asia is weakest, with the Nikkei at -7.7% and Shanghai at -1.8%.

Europe follows, with the DAX at -4.7% and the Swiss index at -3.0%. The US holds up best: the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.9% and the Russell 2000 lost only 0.6%.

Crypto sits in the middle, with Bitcoin at -3.8% and Solana at -5.0%, so risk appetite is weak even in markets that trade all weekend. The lead-lag read for today's US session is cautious.

Overseas weakness tends to reach US large-cap tech first, and the Nasdaq 100 is already the laggard at home. If Europe and Tokyo stabilize, the US small-cap resilience can hold.

If they keep falling, expect the Russell's gap to the Nasdaq to close from the downside.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The two gauges disagree in a way that makes sense. The Crash Index reads 3 of 10, so price action has stacked up several warning signals.

The VIX spike detector reads tier 0 of 4, with the skew, backwardation and adaptive triggers all off. Prices have weakened, and option buyers are not paying up for protection yet.

That is a coherent state: a slow grind lower where hedging demand stays low. It also leaves room for a catch-up, since cheap protection means any shock hits a market with few hedges.

Two confluences are active that depend on VIX backwardation, and the detector does not show it. Trust the detector for today's volatility level, and watch for the first print that flips the backwardation flag.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
